subject: Compile-time arithmetic expressions
notes: Rule: 'The final result of the arithmetic expression shall be truncated to the integer part of the value as specified in 15.49, INTEGER-PART function, and the resultant value shall be considered to be an integer numeric literal' (--check 7.3.6.3 -> OK §7.3.6.3 3)). EvaluateArithmeticOperand applies decimal.Truncate (toward zero = INTEGER-PART) to an expression's final result only, and emits the integer text as the literal; a SINGLE numeric literal is reclassified (§13.10.3 SR1 / §7.3.11.4 GR5) and keeps its value. Probes: CONSTANT AS 7 / 2 -> 3, -7 / 2 -> -3 (toward zero, not floor), 1.5 + 1 -> 2, 0.9 + 0 -> 0; >>DEFINE V2 AS -7 / 2 then >>IF V2 = -3 selects; >>DEFINE V4 AS 1.5 keeps 1.5 (literal) while >>IF V4 + 0 = 1 selects; >>EVALUATE 9 / 4 >>WHEN 2 selects. Binder stores isInt from the integer text so the constant is an integer literal. Unit Theory pins '7 / 2' -> '3' (GR3, spec-derived); the negative toward-zero edge is probe-only.
